name: Andrew Paradise
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, FIRY Inc. (NYSE: FIRY; rebranded from Skillz Inc. in 2026)
profile: Paradise cofounded Skillz with Casey Chafkin in 2012 (originally as Lookout Gaming), creating real-money skill-based mobile gaming; it went public via SPAC in Dec 2020. In 2026 Skillz was rebranded FIRY, a Las Vegas-based holding company spanning Skillz, AI ad-tech platform RZR (Aarki) and developer backend Beamable. He earlier sold mobile-checkout startup AisleBuyer to Intuit in 2012.
interesting_fact: Skillz employees were required to play at least 35 games per week on the platform. FIRY says Paradise personally holds more than 90 issued patents covering matchmaking, fraud detection and real-time competition systems.
deep_cut_fact: He has said he learned to program at age 7 by editing a video game's configuration file with a hex editor, later writing his first game in Pascal; before startups he worked in private equity at Boston-area buyout firm The Watermill Group.
notes: Company renamed from Skillz to FIRY in 2026; HQ Las Vegas. FIRY blog has an 'Andrew Paradise' category with his letters/shareholder addresses (good prep material). Holds ~86% voting power via dual-class shares.

name: Andrey Blokh
current_role: Private investor; major shareholder of Curaleaf Holdings (described by Curaleaf as a retired CPG entrepreneur, not active in the company)
profile: Blokh was briefly president of Russian oil company Sibneft in the late 1990s, then with a partner consolidated Russian dairy assets into Unimilk, which combined with Danone in 2010 to form Danone Unimilk. He later became an early, large investor in US cannabis operator Curaleaf (public 2018). He is a US citizen who also holds a Russian passport.
interesting_fact: His dairy roll-up Unimilk merged with French food giant Danone in 2010 to create Danone Unimilk, one of Russia's largest dairy businesses.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal or office contact published. Only route is indirect via Curaleaf (where he is a passive holder). Press coverage centres on Abramovich-linked loans to Curaleaf insiders; avoid in outreach. Stake size reported variously (~6% voting to ~21%).

name: Candido Pinheiro Koren de Lima Junior
current_role: Board member, Hapvida Participações e Investimentos (Hapvida NotreDame Intermédica); coordinator of its Commercial Committee
profile: Younger son of Hapvida founder Candido Pinheiro, he was Hapvida's sales and relationship vice president from 2001 to 2021 and sits on the board of the Fortaleza-based health insurer/hospital group, which IPO'd in 2018 and merged with NotreDame Intermédica in 2022. Re-elected to the board in April 2026 (term to the 2028 AGM); also on the innovation, quality-of-care and finance committees.
interesting_fact: Hapvida, founded by his oncologist father in Fortaleza, combined with NotreDame Intermédica to create Brazil's largest health-plan operator; the Pinheiro family remains the controlling shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Business Administration at the State University of Ceará (UECE) and led Hapvida's sales and relationship function for two decades (2001-2021); he now coordinates the board's Commercial Committee.
notes: Low-profile family member; brother Jorge Pinheiro is the public face (CEO transitioning to chair, with CFO Luccas Adib named incoming CEO). Approach via Hapvida corporate channels.

name: Li Xiaomin (李晓旻)
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Wintech Nano-Technology Services (胜科纳米(苏州)股份有限公司, SSE STAR: 688757)
profile: A Peking University microelectronics graduate with a master's in electrical engineering from NUS, Li worked as an R&D engineer at Singapore A*STAR's Institute of Microelectronics before founding a commercial third-party semiconductor failure-analysis lab in Singapore in 2004. He set up Wintech Nano in Suzhou in 2012; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market and serves chipmakers with FIB/TEM/SIMS analysis.
interesting_fact: Wintech Nano is a 'hospital for chips': it diagnoses semiconductor failures with tools such as focused ion beams, TEM and SIMS, and in 2026 launched an AI-driven closed-loop analysis system called iWUDI.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 2001-2004 as an R&D engineer at A*STAR's Institute of Microelectronics in Singapore, then founded his first independent failure-analysis lab there in 2004 at about age 29.
notes: Semiconductor-testing angle (relevant to data-center chip supply chain). Speaks to Chinese media as chairman; Singapore background so English outreach plausible.

name: Su Zengfu (苏增福)
current_role: Founder; chairman of Supor Group (苏泊尔集团, the family holding company, separate from SEB-controlled listed Zhejiang Supor) per last available profiles
profile: Born c.1940-41 in Yuhuan, Zhejiang, Su rose from supply clerk to director of a township pressure-cooker parts factory, then in 1994 co-founded cookware brand Supor with his son Su Xianze; it listed in Shenzhen in 2004 and became China's top pressure-cooker brand. The family sold control to France's Groupe SEB from 2006-2011 and Su moved into stainless faucets, pharma, ports, logistics and property.
interesting_fact: Supor was born of necessity: when Shenyang's 'Shuangxi' cooker maker revoked the trademark his factory had licensed (Dec 1994), the family registered their own brand; 'SUPER' was refused, so on the spot they changed one letter to 'SUPOR'.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he served eight years in the PLA Navy (enlisting in 1960 at 19), then worked as a supply-and-marketing clerk for a commune enterprise in Chenyu town; he was also a deputy to the 10th National People's Congress.
notes: Now about 85-86; no recent (2024-26) news found and no death report found, so alive status unverified. No published personal/office contact; family no longer tied to listed Supor (chaired by SEB's Thierry de La Tour d'Artaise). Son Su Xianze is the more public family member.

name: Fan Hao (范浩)
current_role: Chairman, Nanjing Mloptic Corp. (南京茂莱光学科技股份有限公司, SSE STAR: 688502)
profile: Born 1972, Fan Hao co-controls precision-optics maker Mloptic with Fan Yi (vice chairman & CEO); together they control ~66% of the company. Founded in Nanjing in 1999, Mloptic makes precision optical components, lenses and metrology systems for semiconductor lithography/inspection, life sciences, AR/VR, LiDAR and, increasingly, optical interconnect for AI data centers. He has been chairman since 2015.
interesting_fact: Mloptic now markets optics, optical assembly and metrology for AI data-center optical interconnects, alongside AR headset test systems and semiconductor-equipment optics - a direct link to the podcast's data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family optics business he spent 1994-2001 as a business manager at Jiangsu foreign-trade company 江苏省对外经贸, did an MBA at CEIBS (2001-03), then worked as a project manager at SCHOTT's Shanghai precision-materials trading arm; he holds a doctorate from Durham University (UK).
notes: Wealth shared with Fan Yi (co-actual controller, CEO and legal representative). Strong data-center/photonics fit. Sources: 2025 annual report (cninfo) for bio and IR email.

name: Zou Xichang (邹锡昌)
current_role: Chairman of the board, Hong Kong Changsheng (昌盛) Group Ltd (per profile page; not verified in a second source)
profile: Born 1964 in Meizhou, Guangdong, Zou founded Changsheng Group in Hong Kong in 1992 and used it to develop property in Guangzhou and elsewhere (e.g. Tianxiu Building, Yunxiu Garden, Guangzhou International Trade Plaza). He is also credited with founding industrial-design group Echom (毅昌科技). He served as a standing member of the 12th Guangdong CPPCC.
interesting_fact: His first property project (1991) was the ~85,000 sq m Tianxiu Building and Tianxiu Garden in Guangzhou's old city, after an earlier venture building and selling factory units in Shenzhen's Nanyou industrial zone.
deep_cut_fact: He started in business in 1987 by investing RMB 600,000 (with family and friends' backing) in a partnership carton-printing business; it reportedly earned back its cost in three months.
notes: Only one (low-reliability brand-directory) source found linking Zou Xichang to Changsheng Group; matches Hurun 'Changsheng / real estate' but treat facts as unverified. Last on Hurun in 2022; no recent news found. Holds honorary roles in Hong Kong Meizhou/Hakka associations, which may be an indirect route.

name: George Logothetis
current_role: Executive Chairman, Libra Group (NY/London); chairman of Libra Philanthropies; co-chair of Concordia's Leadership Council
profile: Born in London in 1975 to a Greek shipping family, Logothetis joined father's Lomar Shipping at 18 and was CEO by ~1995. In 2003 he and brother Constantine founded Libra Group, selling ships at the top of the cycle to buy aircraft (Lease Corporation International), then expanding into renewable energy, real estate, hospitality and diversified investments. Manos Kouligkas became CEO in 2022.
interesting_fact: He built Libra by sending trusted shipping lieutenants abroad to start new businesses - telling Fortune it 'ended up with a ship's captain running a $200 million real estate company and a Russian fruit seller who runs six biogas plants in Latvia.'
deep_cut_fact: He takes a three-to-five-month sabbatical every five years, avoiding work email and calls because 'ideas need space to be born'; the idea for Libra's diversification came during a sabbatical spent studying in New York.
notes: Sunday Times listing is shared with brother Constantine. Highly public speaker (Concordia Summit, Oxi Day); Libra has big renewable-energy arm, good podcast fit. Libra warns of impersonation scams - genuine mail only from @libra.com. Avoid referencing his childhood illness.

name: Ke Jiansheng (柯建生)
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder, Suofeiya Home Collection (索菲亚家居, SZSE: 002572); executive director of Guangzhou Suofeiya Investment
profile: Born 1964, Ke co-founded Guangzhou-based Suofeiya in 2003 with Jiang Gangjun; the two are its joint actual controllers. Suofeiya pioneered custom-built wardrobes in China by bringing French brand SOGAL's sliding-door wardrobe technology to Chinese homes, listed in Shenzhen in 2011 as the sector's first A-share company, and added kitchen brand SCHMIDT (司米) and door brand Huahe.
interesting_fact: Suofeiya's brand traces to France's SOGAL (founded 1981 by Hassenfratz); the founders combined French sliding wardrobe doors with made-to-measure fitting, effectively creating China's custom-wardrobe industry.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2003 he has served Suofeiya in turn as supervisor, general manager and director; from 2014 to 2022 he was also vice-chairman of the SCHMIDT (司米) kitchen-cabinet JV, and since 2021 runs its electronics/IT arm, Shenzhen Suofeiya Electronic Information.
notes: Low profile; partner Jiang Gangjun (chairman) is the public face. Bio from Suofeiya 2025 annual report (cninfo). Web search budget ran out during this record; facts drawn from filings.

name: the Zochonis family
current_role: Family descendants of PZ Cussons co-founder George Zochonis; long-standing major shareholders in PZ Cussons plc (LSE: PZC), Manchester
profile: Family entry (Sunday Times, shared with Anthony Green). The fortune stems from Paterson Zochonis, a West African trading house founded in Sierra Leone in 1884 by George Zochonis and George Paterson that became soap and personal-care group PZ Cussons (Imperial Leather, Carex, Original Source). Patriarch Sir John Zochonis (chairman, d. 2013) was a major Manchester philanthropist.
interesting_fact: PZ began as a commodity-trading business in colonial Sierra Leone in 1884, expanded into Nigeria before 1900 and, under Constantine Zochonis, opened factories and shops in Ghana and Kenya; Nigeria remains a core PZ market today.
deep_cut_fact: Sir John Zochonis received the 2009 Prince of Wales Medal for Arts Philanthropy and was called 'possibly the largest giver in the North West', backing Chetham's School of Music, Buxton Festival, the Lowry and Manchester International Festival; the family's Zochonis Charitable Trust continues giving.
notes: Family, not an individual; Sir John Zochonis died 30 Nov 2013 and Lady Brigid Zochonis died Feb 2026. No family member is currently PZ chair/CEO (Caroline Silver chair, Jonathan Myers CEO). Identity of co-listed 'Anthony Green' not researched. Very private; the Zochonis Charitable Trust is the most natural family-facing entity.

name: Robert Rayne
current_role: Chair of the Rayne Trust (sister charity of the Rayne Foundation); property investor
profile: The Hon Robert Rayne (b. 1949) is the eldest son of Max, Lord Rayne, the post-war developer who helped rebuild central London after the Blitz and built London Merchant Securities, which merged with Derwent Valley in 2007 to form FTSE-listed Derwent London. Robert's Sunday Times wealth comes from that property legacy; he now chairs the family's Rayne Trust.
interesting_fact: His father founded the Rayne Foundation in 1962; early grants created the Rayne Institutes linking medical research and hospitals in London, Paris and Edinburgh, and Lord Rayne helped found Darwin College, Cambridge.
deep_cut_fact: The Rayne Trust he chairs, founded by his father in 1965, funds work in Israel and the UK to increase coexistence and reduce conflict and exclusion among disadvantaged communities.
notes: Private; best route is the Rayne Foundation office. His own executive roles (e.g. at London Merchant Securities / Derwent London) were not verified from a reachable source because web search budget was exhausted - check before citing. Trustee list: https://www.raynefoundation.org.uk/about-us/team/
